main_text.p: [?]lizà Papa contra ius & fas in feudum accepit, cū Calabriæ & Apuliæ ducatu: ex quo furto manifestò patratæ sunt multæ cædes. Abeunte hoc Pontifice (Perusij namq; erat) Romani iterum libertatem studentes, Banderesios creabant, magistratus nouos, qui uitæ necisq; potestatem haberent. Senatorem, priuatum hominem quendam Brancaleonem Bononiensem elegerunt: quem paulo post fu-gatum, iterum revocarunt. Pauca præter ea, quæ iam dicta sunt, Vrbanus fecit: nisi quòd cuiusdam fœminæ instinctu, festum Eucharistici panis, seu triticei Dei, quod Corporis Christi uocant, quintā feriā post Trinitatis festum instituerit, cum processionibus, facibus, uexillis, conopæis, Missarum solennitatibus, & octauis. Quibus maximas indulgentias didit indulgentias, ut præ cæteris diis omnibus coleretur deus Mauzim. Eiusq; efficium ex veteris Testamenti figuris & umbris, per Thomam Aquinatem Dominicanorum doctorem sanctum fabri-cari iussit.

Multæ sunt opiniones, super prima huius festi origine: sed hanc accipe certiorem esse, ex Arnoldo Bostio, ac Petro Præmonstratensi. Anno Domini 1264. revelatio sanè diabolica, super hoc sacramenti festo celebrando, cuidam Euæ fœminæ Leodiensi, in otia superstitioso reclusæ.

page.notes: The first word of the page is partly damaged at the left edge; "lizà" is uncertain. The word "Abeunte" is read from a faint line, and the middle of the sentence "quibus maximas indulgentias" is partly overprinted by the next line, so the transcription there is doubtful. The word "ocia" was read as "otia" by correction, and the printed form may differ. Catchword "Pontifi" is partly cut off. The signature "V 3" is at the foot left. The page is heavily stained at the left margin, with no marginal notes visible.
